original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-localize-cartesian-square}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r] & X \ar[d] \\
Y' \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\mathcal{C}$. Then we have
$j_{Y'/Y}^{-1} \circ Rj_{X/Y, *} = Rj_{X'/Y', *} \circ j_{X'/X}^{-1}$
as functors $D(\mathcal{C}/X) \to D(\mathcal{C}/Y')$.

final_content.statement:
For a morphism $X\to Y$ in a site $\mathcal C$, write $j_{X/Y}:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/Y)$ for the localization morphism of topoi; on a ringed site it induces the corresponding morphism of ringed topoi. The restriction functors $j^{-1}$ (abelian sheaves) and $j^*$ (ringed-module sheaves) are exact. Consider a cartesian square $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ in $\mathcal C$. The cohomology statement is in derived categories of **abelian sheaves**, without assuming any ringed structure and without assuming the square is an open-immersion square.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r] & X \ar[d] \\
Y' \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\mathcal{C}$. Then we have
$j_{Y'/Y}^{-1} \circ Rj_{X/Y, *} = Rj_{X'/Y', *} \circ j_{X'/X}^{-1}$
as functors $D(\mathcal{C}/X) \to D(\mathcal{C}/Y')$.
hypotheses: $X'\to X$, $X'\to Y'$, $X\to Y$, $Y'\to Y$ form a cartesian square in $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: There is a canonical base-change isomorphism $j_{Y'/Y}^{-1}\circ Rj_{X/Y,*}\cong Rj_{X'/Y',*}\circ j_{X'/X}^{-1}$ of functors $D(\mathcal C/X)\to D(\mathcal C/Y')$.

semantic_review_note: In a cartesian square of objects of an arbitrary site, the localized derived pushforward for abelian sheaves commutes with exact restriction j^{-1}; all four localization functors and variance D(C/X)→D(C/Y') are preserved, without needing ringed structure.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-localize-cartesian-square-modules}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r] & X \ar[d] \\
Y' \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\mathcal{C}$. Then we have
$j_{Y'/Y}^* \circ Rj_{X/Y, *} = Rj_{X'/Y', *} \circ j_{X'/X}^*$
as functors
$D(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D(\mathcal{O}_{Y'})$.

final_content.statement:
For a morphism $X\to Y$ in a site $\mathcal C$, write $j_{X/Y}:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/Y)$ for the localization morphism of topoi; on a ringed site it induces the corresponding morphism of ringed topoi. The restriction functors $j^{-1}$ (abelian sheaves) and $j^*$ (ringed-module sheaves) are exact. For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ and cartesian square of objects, the slice sites inherit ring sheaves $\mathcal O_X$ etc. The isomorphism concerns the ordinary exact restriction $j^*$ on **module derived categories**, not the inverse-image $j^{-1}$ used for abelian sheaves.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[d] \ar[r] & X \ar[d] \\
Y' \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\mathcal{C}$. Then we have
$j_{Y'/Y}^* \circ Rj_{X/Y, *} = Rj_{X'/Y', *} \circ j_{X'/X}^*$
as functors
$D(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D(\mathcal{O}_{Y'})$.
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.
$X'=X\times_Y Y'$ forms a cartesian square of objects of $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: There is a canonical isomorphism $j_{Y'/Y}^*\circ Rj_{X/Y,*}\cong Rj_{X'/Y',*}\circ j_{X'/X}^*$ of functors $D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_{Y'})$.

semantic_review_note: For a cartesian object square in a RINGED site, the module-derived pushforward base-change isomorphism uses j^* instead of j^{-1} and correctly lands in D(O_{Y'}), with all slice rings retained.
